summary.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; FY27 guidance is early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore and PBT before exceptional items rose 16.8% to INR87 crore, driven by volume growth and better mix. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% in Q4, Astec reached EBITDA break-even for the year, and Crop Care was hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, with the Iran war and a weak monsoon forecast flagged as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, well ahead of industry; cattle feed +24%. Margins expanded, helped by new Type 1 products, East and Central share gains, raw material cost reconfiguration, and a ~INR9.5 crore pet food manufacturing income booked in other income.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 marked by record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (~60,000 t of FFB out of 6.37 lakh t annually) but margins held. Specialty fat refinery to start rolling out in May 2026.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 hit by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 is guided as a recovery year, with recovery from Q2 and very high double-digit growth in top and bottom line.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA break-even in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realisations and utilisation. FY26 mix was ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO; exports ~53% of revenue. Board reconstituted with Arijit Mukherjee as Executive Director.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy (CDPL)
segments.commentary: Revenue ~5% YoY ex bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Management expects milk prices to ease gradually from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading is being phased out; momos and frozen chicken entries planned.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth targeted at early double-digit, volume-led.
FY27 consolidated PBT growth targeted at mid-teens (described as mid-strong double-digit, mid-teens).
Animal Nutrition: double-digit volume-led revenue growth targeted in FY27.
Crop Care: FY27 a recovery year, with very high double-digit top and bottom line growth expected; full recovery from Q2.
Astec: top-line growth around 15% targeted, CDMO growing faster; CDMO salience guided to 52-53%+, with ~20% growth aspiration mentioned.
FY27 capex around INR350-400 crore (about 75-80% growth capex, ~50% to oil palm); post-capex cash surplus around INR100-125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and PBT outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated early double-digit revenue growth, volume-led, and mid-strong double-digit (mid-teens) PBT growth; the Iran war is the main overhang.

qa_highlights.question: How does a below-normal monsoon (IMD/Skymet El Nino forecasts) affect the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance stands for now; the severe impact is expected in August-September, and Crop Care's skew to South and West may be less affected. Oil palm is not expected to see an impact this year, with possible effects next year.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Astec's raw material comes from China, and how is currency managed?
qa_highlights.answer: About 47% of total imports came from China last year. Being a net exporter, the currency impact is described as roughly neutral, with a possible mild positive.

qa_highlights.question: What is behind the Animal Nutrition volume acceleration and margin sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are East and Central share gains, Type 1 higher-yield products, and raw material reconfiguration. The Rs9.5 crore pet food income sits in other income as a contract manufacturing profit, with no revenue recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Astec structure or chemicals business change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on structure; a decision is expected over the next two to three quarters. Arijit Mukherjee was elevated to Executive Director and COO-led growth continues.

qa_highlights.question: What is the oil palm outlook if palm prices correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing contributed about 30% of last year's profit jump; the specialty fat refinery and a 50-55% value-added target by FY31 are meant to cushion volatility.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the payout has been around 48% and is decided with promoters as results come in; no commitment was made.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at roughly INR350-400 crore; about 75-80% is growth capex and roughly 50% of capex goes to oil palm.
FY27 post-capex cash surplus expected at about INR100-125 crore.

Oil palm: record area expansion in FY26; management aims to beat that record area expansion in FY27. About 50% of trees are juvenile (0-4 years, unproductive), which management expects to become productive over the next five years.
Oil palm specialty fat refinery rolls out in May 2026, reaching full flow in the second half of FY27; target of 50-55% of oil palm portfolio from value-added products by about FY31.

Astec: CDMO share guided to 52-53%+ of revenue; FY26 mix ~48% enterprise and ~52% CDMO, with the enterprise share expected to fall only after FY28. Export share ~53% in FY26, expected around 60% if enterprise molecules move up.
Crop Care: two new products (Ashitaka maize herbicide, launched December 2025; TAKAI rice-plus-insecticide) expected to contribute roughly 16-18% of Crop Care revenue in FY27, versus ~3% last year.
demand_pricing: Animal Nutrition: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, cattle feed +24%; management attributes gains to new Type 1 products, share gains in East and Central India, and raw material cost reconfiguration. FY27 target is double-digit volume-led revenue growth.
Milk procurement costs elevated, pushing farmers toward branded compound feed; management expects milk prices to ease from Q2 FY27.

Crop Care: Q4 volumes hit by co-marketing channel inventory carry-forward; roughly a Q1 FY27 impact as that inventory clears; full recovery expected from Q2 FY27 with very high double-digit top and bottom-line growth.

Oil palm: Q4 OER 20.77% vs 19.76% a year earlier on about 60,000 t of FFB (out of 6.37 lakh t annually). Management is guiding early double-digit volume growth in FY27 and says FY26 pricing gains were about 30% of the profit jump, the rest from internal efforts.

Astec: Q4 price realisations and volumes improved; management says prices have bottomed and China competitiveness has stabilised. FY27 top-line growth target around 15%, with CDMO growing faster and a ~20% aspiration. Margins described as intact.
Creamline Dairy: Q4 revenue ~5% YoY excluding bulk sales; value-added salience ~40% vs 38%; profitability under pressure from milk costs.
Godrej Foods: EBITDA margins improved in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded salience above 80% in FY26; live bird trading being phased out.
risks_watch: Below-normal monsoon, with IMD and Skymet forecasts of a weak August-September; management says the impact on Animal Nutrition is tied to milk yields.
Iran war and crude-linked palm oil price volatility; management says it is playing palm oil quarter to quarter.
Crop Care Q1 FY27 carry-forward inventory clearance and whether recovery starts from Q2 as guided.
Astec structure review (decision in two to three quarters) and the chemicals-group restructuring, with strategic reviews of Shrimp, Seeds and Cattle Genetics businesses.
Creamline milk procurement costs, with expected easing from Q2 FY27.
Monitor the FY27 new-product ramp (Ashitaka, TAKAI) and the specialty fat refinery rollout in May 2026.

summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 volume-led growth and Animal Nutrition, and on oil palm and Astec. Cautious and evasive on the monsoon, palm oil prices, and the Astec structure, where management said it is too early to decide.

adds.what: Oil palm specialty fat refinery (value-added products)
Oil palm record area expansion; aim to beat FY26 record in FY27 (planted area, not yet productive; ~50% of trees juvenile)

growth.why: FY27 guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue (~10% midpoint) and mid-teens PBT growth, backed by Animal Nutrition volume gains (+15% Q4), Crop Care recovery from Q2 and new products, but no specific order book or capacity numbers were given to back the guidance; capex of INR350-400 crore (75-80% growth) is held with timing largely unspecified.
